section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a single community sample (no label such as 'Study 1') of 156 women and 144 men (total N = 300) recruited in Vienna and its environs. Mean ages are reported separately by gender (women M = 31.66, men M = 33.31) and mean BMIs are given for women (M = 21.94) and men (M = 24.01); educational attainment and religious affiliation percentages are also provided. No information is given about survey method, ethnicity/percent white, BMI assessment method (measured vs self-reported), body appreciation assessment, or any correlations between body appreciation and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: Full section text: 'Participants were a community sample of 156 women and 144 men, ranging in age from 16 to 80 years (age M \pm SD women = 31.66 \pm 13.60, men = 33.31 \pm = 15.05). Data collection took place in Vienna and its environs, and represents volunteers from the general population. The mean body mass index (BMI) for male participants was 24.01 kg/m^2 (SD = 3.34, range 17.81-36.92 kg/m^2), whereas that of women was 21.94 kg/m^2 (SD = 3.82, range 16.33-45.91 kg/m^2), ... In terms of highest educational qualification, the majority of participants were educated to a secondary level (68.0%; university = 14.3%, apprenticeships = 10.3%, primary school = 7.0%).'
